name: The Content Engine: Solo Founder Edition
tagline: Turn a single raw idea into a full week of high-converting social media posts in minutes.
metaDescription: Stop staring at a blank screen. Use these 12 plug-and-play AI prompts to transform one core business idea into a full week of engaging posts for solo founders.
description:
Running a startup alone means your most scarce resource is time, yet consistent publishing is non-negotiable for growth. **The Content Engine** is built specifically for solo founders who need to build in public and attract customers without spending hours writing copy.

This prompt pack solves the blank-page syndrome by taking one raw concept—a feature launch, a customer insight, or a daily frustration—and systematically breaking it down into platform-specific angles. These prompts work because they leverage established copywriting frameworks (like PAS and AIDA) combined with platform-native formatting rules, ensuring your content sounds human, authoritative, and engaging.

Whether you are marketing a bootstrapped SaaS, an agency, or a digital product, these structured prompts help you maintain a daily publishing habit across LinkedIn, X, and newsletters in under 30 minutes a week.
includes: 1 Notion template containing all 12 tested prompts
1 Markdown file for local AI chat apps
12 distinct prompt workflows across 4 strategic categories
Usage tips and output examples for every single prompt
sampleItems: Act as an expert B2B copywriter. Take my raw product update and rewrite it into a short, punchy LinkedIn post using the Hook-Value-CTA framework.
Analyze my startup's biggest recent user win and draft a 5-part X thread that breaks down the exact steps we took to achieve it.

items.title: The Origin Story Hook
items.body: Act as an experienced startup storyteller. Take my raw idea or product feature and write 3 distinct opening hooks for a LinkedIn post. The first hook should use a counterintuitive statement, the second should highlight a painful solo founder frustration, and the third should share an unexpected metric or milestone. Keep each hook under 20 words. Ensure they are designed to stop the scroll without using cheap clickbait tactics, setting up a genuine narrative about building in public.

items.title: The Thread Architect
items.body: Act as a growth marketer specializing in X threads. Take my core business insight and expand it into a high-retention 6-part thread. Tweet 1 must hook the reader with the core problem. Tweets 2 through 4 must deliver actionable frameworks, bullet points, or step-by-step lessons. Tweet 5 should share a relevant real-world example or mini-case study. Tweet 6 must end with a clear call-to-action inviting engagement or newsletter sign-ups. Use short paragraphs and high-whitespace formatting throughout.

items.title: The Pain-Agitate-Solve Post
items.body: Act as a direct-response copywriter. Take my product's primary value proposition and structure a short-form post using the PAS (Problem-Agitate-Solve) framework. First, state the silent frustration my target customer feels every day. Second, agitate that problem by explaining the hidden costs in wasted time and money. Third, introduce my product as the effortless, elegant solution. Keep the total word count under 120 words and write in a conversational, empathetic tone suitable for indie hackers.

items.title: The Behind-the-Scenes Breakdown
items.body: Act as a transparent startup advisor. Take a recent challenge, metric, or failure from my solo founder journey and draft a 'build in public' post. Break the post down into three sections: 1) What we tried, 2) Why it completely failed or fell short, and 3) The exact lesson learned and what we are doing differently starting today. Avoid toxic positivity; focus on raw, pragmatic lessons that other bootstrap founders will respect, bookmark, and share.

items.title: The Myth vs. Reality Contrast
items.body: Act as a contrarian industry analyst. Take a common industry best practice or piece of startup advice that I disagree with, and write a LinkedIn post contrasting 'What most founders think' with 'What actually works'. Use clear formatting with bullet points. Provide a brief justification for my contrarian stance based on real-world bootstrapping experience. The tone should be authoritative yet approachable, designed to spark respectful debate in the comments section.

items.title: The Customer Insight Spotlight
items.body: Act as a SaaS copywriter. Take a piece of raw feedback, a glowing review, or a support ticket from a happy user, and transform it into a case-study style post. Highlight the customer's initial state of confusion or inefficiency, the turning point when they adopted our solution, and their current workflow transformation. Conclude with a subtle nod to our product without sounding overly salesy. Focus heavily on the human impact of the software.

items.title: The Mini-Tutorial Framework
items.body: Act as a technical educator. Take a complex process related to my niche and break it down into an easy-to-digest 3-step mini-tutorial. Format each step with a clear action verb, a concise explanation, and a common pitfall to avoid. The post must deliver immediate, standalone value to the reader even if they never buy my product, establishing my brand as a trusted, generous subject matter expert in the market.

items.title: The Future Prediction Post
items.body: Act as a market forecaster in my specific niche. Take a current trend I am noticing among my users and project its impact over the next 12 to 24 months. Write a visionary short post outlining two things that will become obsolete soon and one skill or tool that will become mandatory for survival. Use clean spacing and an optimistic, forward-looking tone that positions my solo venture at the cutting edge of the industry.

items.title: The Newsletter Teaser
items.body: Act as an email marketing specialist. Take the main topic of my latest weekly newsletter edition and write 3 teaser posts tailored for social media. Each teaser must highlight a surprising statistic, a provocative question, or a deep insight from the essay, followed by a direct link to the full archive. Ensure the tease creates an irresistible information gap that compels busy professionals to click through and read more.

items.title: The FAQ Objection Crusher
items.body: Act as a conversion rate optimization expert. Take the number one objection or hesitation potential customers have before buying my product (e.g., price, time to value, complexity) and write a post addressing it head-on. Validate their concern, dismantle the assumption with logical proof, and show how our product mitigates the risk. Keep the argument sharp, respectful, and entirely focused on ROI for solo operators.

items.title: The Weekly Round-Up & Wins
items.body: Act as a community manager. Write a concise Friday wrap-up post for my startup journey. Include placeholders for one shipping milestone, one metric update (revenue, users, or traffic), and one personal takeaway or habit that kept me sane this week. End with a lighthearted question to my followers wishing them a great weekend. This humanizes the brand and drives high comment engagement.

items.title: The Contrarian Takeaway
items.body: Act as an X ghostwriter. Take a standard piece of advice in my niche and distill it into a single, high-impact one-liner followed by a 3-sentence explanation. The formatting must rely on extreme whitespace and ultra-short sentences. The goal is to maximize retweets and bookmark saves by providing a crystal-clear paradigm shift that readers can immediately apply to their daily workflow.
